title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from this and the neighbouring pages. L is an ordered set, apparently totally ordered: a combinatorial 'line'. 𝔘 is a set of 'strata' built from L: points a ∈ L and interstitial open intervals I_{a,b} between consecutive points. The completion 𝔘̂ adds the unbounded strata I_{<a} and I_{>b}. 𝔘̂ carries an order ≤ (X ≤ Y meaning X lies to the left of Y, or equal). It also carries an incidence relation X ◁ Y, read as 'X is a boundary point of Y'. The previous page proved a density lemma: 𝔘 is 'very dense' in 𝔘̂ for a separation relation |∘|.

This page sets up the combinatorics of finite 'generalized polyfigures'.

(1) Definition. A 𝔘̂-polyfigure Φ is a finite totally ordered subset (a chain, or 'flag') of (𝔘̂, ≤), i.e. a finite family of pairwise disjoint, linearly ordered cells.

(2) The boundary flag. To Φ one attaches δΦ = T^Φ ∈ Drap*(L), the flag of L formed by all points of L that occur in Φ either as members or as endpoints of its intervals. The marginal note adds that δΦ is empty iff Φ is empty.

(3) Strata of a flag. For a flag T = {t1 < … < tn} of L, the generalized interstitial strata are
[I_{<t1}], t1, I_{t1,t2}, t2, …, tn, [I_{>tn}].
The bracketed end-intervals appear only when t1 is not minimal, resp. tn is not maximal. In modern terms this is the cell decomposition of the line induced by finitely many points. These strata form the largest polyfigure Φ̂ with δΦ̂ = T.

(4) Classification. A nonempty Φ is equivalent to the data of (T, S), where T is a flag and S is a set of strata of T such that every t ∈ T either lies in S or is a boundary point (t ◁ X) of some X ∈ S. This is the 1-dimensional case of 'a finite subcomplex is determined by its cells, and its vertex set must be exactly the vertices used'.

Purpose. The next page defines the complement 𝔓* = 𝔓̂ ∖ 𝔓 and computes δ𝔓* = δ𝔓 ∖ 𝔓_red, where 𝔓_red is the set of redundant vertices (vertices of order 2). It then studies the double complement 𝔓**, a regularization that removes redundant vertices. So the page is foundational bookkeeping for a combinatorial calculus of 1-dimensional 'figures' (finite unions of points and intervals) and their complements. This is in the spirit of a tame or combinatorial topology of the line, which the 'Ateliers' chapters use to build up 'polygons'/'polyfigures'.
errors: No real mathematical error. The classification in (4) tacitly uses two facts: every endpoint of an interval in Φ automatically lies in T = δΦ (true by definition of δ), and the strata of a flag are pairwise disjoint and linearly ordered, so every subset of them is again a chain (true).

The claim 'δΦ empty iff Φ empty' requires that the whole line L is not itself a stratum of 𝔘̂. This holds with the strata listed, since every element of 𝔘̂ involves at least one point of L, but it is not stated.
The parenthetical 'cf. ...' after 'non maximal' is not readable; it may point to the conventions of earlier pages.

ideas.what: Finite chains in the completed stratum poset 𝔘̂ as 'generalized polyfigures', with boundary flag δΦ in Drap*(L)
ideas.modern_name: finite 1-dimensional cell complexes / finite unions of points and open intervals in an ordered set (definable sets in dimension 1 of an o-minimal structure)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (cell decompositions); o-minimal formulation: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn (1984–86)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) calls for a 'topologie modérée' in general terms, but this combinatorial formalism is not published there

ideas.what: Interstitial strata of a flag T = {t1<…<tn}: the stratification of the line into points and the open intervals between them, unbounded ends included only if t1 / tn are non-extremal
ideas.modern_name: stratification (cell decomposition) of an ordered line induced by a finite set

ideas.what: Bijection between nonempty polyfigures and pairs (flag T, set of strata S covering every t ∈ T either as a member or as a boundary point)
ideas.modern_name: description of a subcomplex by its cells, with a vertex-incidence (closure-of-support) condition

missed.claim: The surrounding pages (complement 𝔓*, double complement 𝔓**, removal of redundant vertices of order 2) amount to a combinatorial regularization calculus for 1-dimensional definable figures. This is close to the Boolean algebra of regular open sets and to cell decomposition in o-minimal dimension 1, and in the same years Grothendieck advocated 'topologie modérée'. This page, though, is only basic set-up.
missed.quote: Ce sont les strates de la plus grande 𝔘̂-polyfigure possible Φ̂, telle que δΦ̂ = T.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only as historical evidence of Grothendieck working, in 1986, on a hands-on combinatorial foundation for tame 1-dimensional figures, contemporaneous with o-minimality. The mathematics on this page itself is elementary and well known.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary, correct set-up of the combinatorics of finite cell decompositions of an ordered line. Interest is purely historical, as a glimpse of Grothendieck's late combinatorial 'tame geometry' notes; nothing here is new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Opening line is likely 'Mais c'est à l'aune des rapports pour 𝔘 générique [que l'on] s'intéresse en fait !', not 'Mais cela à l'aune ...'; reading tentative.
The symbol is 𝔘̂ (U with hat) throughout, including in 'des figures et polyfigures finies de 𝔘̂' and '𝔘̂-polyfigures'.
The left margin note reads roughly 'bien entendu le drapeau T^Φ est vide ssi Φ est vide' / 'non vide'. It is the marginal counterpart of the inserted phrase after Drap*(L).
'(i.e., il existe < t1)' is an insertion over 't1 non minimal' and reads '(i.e., il n'existe pas ... )' / 'il existe <t1'; the transcription's reading is acceptable.
'ayant la propriété suivante' is preceded by the deleted words 'strates intrinsèques'. 'L[a] donnée d'un Φ ≠ ∅' sits after the deleted '𝔘̂-polyfigure' line.
